rationale: Round 1 built and ran correctly with no ICE fallback, so this round pushes obfuscation intensity up while protecting linpack's hot numeric kernels (daxpy, dmxpy, dgefa, dgesl), where loop-carried float operations dominate runtime. SUB gets the highest Security/Diversity weights since arithmetic substitution is cheap, correct, and directly obscures the FLOP-heavy inner loops; SPLIT and IBR follow, as basic-block splitting and indirect branching add strong control-flow confusion with low cost and low risk, making them safe to apply broadly including main. BCF and FLA keep high RuntimeCost weights so the selector steers them away from the tight inner-loop functions and toward colder code (main, setup/reporting paths), bounding runtime overhead while still flattening/bogifying whatever regions tolerate it. ICALL and IGV raise Diversity to frustrate cross-procedure static analysis of the BLAS helper call graph, with moderate IGV CorrectnessRisk weight retained because global-variable encoding touches more of the module and round 1 gave no signal that extra risk there is free. Overall: aggressive low-cost passes, cost-gated aggressive passes, and correctness risk kept low everywhere since the measured pipeline is stable but the kernel is numerically sensitive.
